## Also in the box

  * `EgressGuard` — an outbound allowlist to wrap any request a tool makes. A tool reaching a host you never listed is the classic phone-home tell. `*.example.com` matches subdomains; an empty allowlist blocks everything rather than allowing everything.
  * `isSensitiveTool` / `classifyTools` — glob classification of tools that must require per-call approval. Sensitive tools stay advertised; they just cannot run unattended.
  * `canonicalize` / `parseJsonStrict` — a strict RFC 8785 (JCS) implementation, also exported as `@aimarket/warden/jcs` so another implementation can be byte-checked against it. Integers only beyond `MAX_SAFE_JSON_INTEGER`, refusal (not escaping) on lone surrogates, and a reason code on every refusal.

# Tokenade documentation

Updated October 16, 2026

TL;DR — Install with `npm install -g @tokenade/cli`, then run `tokenade install`. From then on Tokenade works in the background of your coding agent.

Tokenade cuts the token bill of AI coding agents: one install, zero config, and it trims what your agent sends to the model.

Tokenade is a local command-line tool that sits between your AI coding agent and its tools, and trims what the agent would otherwise send to the model: long command output, whole files, web pages, verbose MCP results. It plugs into each agent through that agent's own hooks, plugins or MCP configuration, so you keep working exactly as before. Everything is folded on your machine, and anything folded can be recovered byte for byte.

## Quickstart

You need Node.js 18 or later. Tokenade is free and open source (MIT/Apache-2.0).

Copy

npm install -g @tokenade/cli
tokenade install

  * `npm install -g @tokenade/cli` downloads the prebuilt binary for your platform. See Install Tokenade.

# Install Tokenade

Updated October 16, 2026

TL;DR — Run `npm install -g @tokenade/cli` (Node 18+), then `tokenade install` without sudo. Preview first with `tokenade install --dry-run`.

To install Tokenade, install the npm package globally, then run `tokenade install` once as your normal user. The first command puts the binary on your machine; the second connects it to the coding agents it finds.

Copy

npm install -g @tokenade/cli
tokenade install

That's all: there is nothing to activate. Tokenade is free and open source (MIT/Apache-2.0); the code is on GitHub.

Prefer to let your agent do it? Paste this into your coding agent: "Install Tokenade for me: read https://tokenade.net/install.md and follow the instructions."

## Requirements

  * Node.js 18 or later (only for the npm installer; Tokenade itself is a native binary).
  * One of the supported platforms:

OS  | Architectures
--- | ---
Linux  | x64 (glibc and musl), arm64 (musl)
macOS  | Apple Silicon (arm64), Intel (x64)
Windows  | x64, arm64

## What the npm package does

`@tokenade/cli` ships one optional dependency per platform. npm installs the one matching your machine, and the `postinstall` step uses it directly (`tokenade provided by @tokenade/cli-... — no download needed`).

If that platform package is missing, `postinstall` falls back to downloading the binary from the matching GitHub Release, verifies the release manifest against its Ed25519 signature, checks the archive's SHA-256 against that signed manifest, and checks that the file really is an executable for your OS before keeping it.

The download honours your proxy settings and has a timeout:

Variable  | Effect
--- | ---
`HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` (and lowercase forms)  | Route the download through your proxy
`NO_PROXY` / `no_proxy`  | Hosts that bypass the proxy
`TOKENADE_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS`  | Per-request timeout in milliseconds (default `30000`)

Network errors are retried; a 4xx response (other than 429) or a checksum mismatch is not.

Check the binary:

Copy

tokenade --version

Copy

tokenade 2.0.1

## Upgrading from 1.x

If auto-update is on (the default), your 1.x install moves to 2.0 by itself. Otherwise, run:

Copy

npm i -g @tokenade/cli@latest

The licence and account files left by 1.x are cleaned up during the upgrade.

## What `tokenade install` does

`tokenade install` is zero-config. In one run it:

  1. Detects the coding agents installed on the machine (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Kilo Code, and the others listed in compatibility).
  2. Wires Tokenade into each one through that agent's own mechanism: hooks for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Grok, Droid and the Antigravity CLI; a plugin or extension for OpenCode, Kilo Code, Cline, Hermes, Pi and OpenClaw.
  3. Writes a short Tokenade rules section into the global rules file each agent loads (for example `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `~/.codex/AGENTS.md`), and scaffolds project rules in the current folder.
  4. Routes your third-party MCP servers through `tokenade mcp-wrap`, so their large results are folded. See Wrap MCP servers.
  5. Sets up the local LLM proxy for an agent only where it adds a feature the agent's hooks cannot provide (for example Codex while its hooks are not approved). It binds `127.0.0.1` and prints how to undo it.
  6. Enables `~/.tokenade/debug.log`, which `tokenade hooks tail` reads.

Every config file it edits is merged, not replaced: your own hooks, MCP servers and rules stay as they are. Each agent page lists the exact files: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot.

### Do not use sudo

Run `tokenade install` as yourself. Under `sudo` it refuses, because it would write into `/root` and your agent would never see the hooks:

Copy

✗ running under sudo: this would install into /root, not your own HOME —
your AI agent would never see the hooks (and everything would LOOK fine).
Re-run WITHOUT sudo: tokenade install
(intentional root install: TOKENADE_ALLOW_ROOT=1 tokenade install)

For a deliberate root install, set `TOKENADE_ALLOW_ROOT=1`.

### Preview before writing

Copy

tokenade install --dry-run

`--dry-run` prints every file it would change, including the Codex `config.toml` trust entries, and writes nothing.
`--defaults`  | Forget the choices remembered from earlier installs

Agent names accepted by `--only`: `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `copilot`, `kilo-code`, `opencode`, `cline`, `hermes`, `pi`, `openclaw`, `qwen-code`, `antigravity`, `grok`, `droid`, `aider`, `t3-code`, `devin-desktop` (`windsurf` is a deprecated alias of `devin-desktop`). `--only` narrows the detected agents to one: if that agent is not found on the machine, install stops and suggests the closest detected name.

Copy

tokenade install --only claude-code # just Claude Code
tokenade install --per-project # ./.claude/ instead of ~/.claude/

### Remembered choices

Install remembers the opt-outs and choices you pass (`--no-hook`, `--only`, `--per-project`, `--no-debug-log`, `--debug-log`, `--no-autocompact`, `--no-wrap-mcps`, `--profile`, `--with-*`). Every later install, upgrade and self-repair reuses them. To start again from the defaults:

Copy

tokenade install --defaults

### Other token tools

Install also looks for other token-saving tools that conflict with Tokenade and proposes fixes. Run the check on its own with `tokenade incompatibilities`, or skip the fix-up pass with `--no-cleanup`.

## Re-running install

`tokenade install` is idempotent. Re-run it after installing a new agent, or when `tokenade healthcheck` reports something missing. Updates refresh the hooks and plugins on their own; see Upgrade and uninstall.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Files and paths

Updated October 7, 2026

TL;DR — Tokenade's state lives in ~/.tokenade/ (%USERPROFILE%\.tokenade on Windows); stashed outputs and the embedding model live in ~/.cache/tokenade/ (%LOCALAPPDATA%\tokenade on Windows). A project can hold .tokenade/filters/. `tokenade uninstall` removes both trees.

Tokenade keeps everything it owns in two directories in your home: a state directory, `~/.tokenade/`, and a cache directory, `~/.cache/tokenade/`. Besides those, it writes its hooks and rules into your agents' own config files. Nothing is stored anywhere else unless you point it there with an environment variable.

## The two trees, per OS

 | Linux  | macOS  | Windows
--- | --- | --- | ---
State  | `~/.tokenade/`  | `~/.tokenade/`  | `%USERPROFILE%\.tokenade\`
Cache  | `~/.cache/tokenade/`  | `~/.cache/tokenade/`  | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\tokenade\`

How they are resolved:

  * Home: `$HOME` on Linux and macOS. On Windows, `%USERPROFILE%` comes first, because `HOME` is usually unset there (only Git Bash and MSYS2 set it).

# Frequently asked questions

Everything you need to know about Tokenade — compatibility, privacy, open source licence, and setup.

What is Tokenade?
    Tokenade is a local, open-source tool that automatically cuts the token usage of AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Kilo Code, Devin Desktop, Cline, and more). Plugged into your agent, it filters noisy shell output, gives it file skeletons and semantic search so it stops reading whole files, and compacts MCP server output (with dedicated handling for GitHub, Playwright, Postgres and other popular servers) — without touching your code.

Which agents and IDEs does Tokenade work with?
    Tokenade plugs into each agent through its own hooks, plugins or rules files, not through MCP: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code), Cline, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf), Qwen Code, Grok, Droid, Aider and more. How much is covered depends on the agent (see the compatibility page in the docs). OS support: Linux, macOS, and Windows.

How much does Tokenade cost?
    Nothing. Tokenade is free and open source (MIT/Apache-2.0), for everyone, on as many machines as you like.

How many machines can I use?
    As many as you like: install the CLI on each machine and you're done.

Which operating systems does Tokenade support?
    Linux, macOS, and Windows are all officially supported. Installation goes through npm, which fetches the prebuilt native binary for your platform.

How do I install Tokenade?
    Two commands: `npm install -g @tokenade/cli`, then `tokenade install`. The second detects your agents and configures them automatically (hooks or plugins, plus wrapping of your MCP servers).

How many tokens does Tokenade actually save?
    Savings depend on the agent and project. On THOL's long sessions, an agent running Tokenade costs 39% less than the same agent on its own. `tokenade dashboard` opens a local report of your real savings in your browser, to explore in detail.

Is Tokenade open source?
    Yes. The code is dual-licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0, at your option: https://github.com/pi-infected/tokenade. Audit it, fork it, and contribute — issues and pull requests are welcome.

How is Tokenade different from other token optimizers?
    Most optimizers work at the prompt level (truncation, summarization). Tokenade works at the tool boundary: through your agent's hooks or plugins, it compacts what tools return (shell output, file reads, web pages, documents, MCP results) and gives the agent compact tools of its own (skeleton, semantic search, `tokenade read`). Failures, numbers and decisive lines are kept, and the full output stays recoverable — not an approximate summary.

I paid for Tokenade — what happens?
    Subscriptions are cancelled and nothing more is billed. Auto-update moves your CLI to 2.0 and your account data is deleted. Questions? Email [email protected].

# About Tokenade

Tokenade makes AI coding affordable by automatically cutting the tokens your agents consume — without changing how you work.

## Who we are

Tokenade is built by Paul Irolla, an independent developer who got tired of watching AI coding bills spiral month after month. The mission is simple: make the productivity gains of AI coding accessible to every developer, not just those with a generous expense account.

Paul Irolla

Founder · AI & developer tools

## Why we built it

Modern AI coding agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Windsurf — are powerful, but they are voracious token consumers. Every file read, every tool call, every context window refill adds up. A productive day of AI-assisted coding can quietly burn through tens of millions of tokens.

We built Tokenade to make token reduction automatic and measurable. Instead of manually pruning context or guessing which calls are expensive, Tokenade intercepts the flow — semantic code search replaces full-file reads, output filtering strips noise before it reaches the model, skeleton compression shrinks large files to signatures, and lazy MCP loading defers tools until they are actually needed. The savings dashboard shows you exactly how much you saved and what it cost before.

## What makes Tokenade different

  * 1

Works with every major AI coding agent — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Windsurf — via a single MCP server layer, zero per-agent configuration.

  * 2

Source-available (MIT licence): you can read every line, run it locally, and trust it with your codebase.

  * 3

Freemium: free up to ~10 million tokens saved per month, then Pro at $24.90/mo excl. tax (100M tokens) — pay only when the savings are real.
